readerA.quote: Single crystal specimens of composition 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20 atom percent thallium, and polycrystalline specimens containing 15, 20, 38, and 50 percent thallium, were investigated. ... The critical fields for destruction of superconductivity are given for the range 0 to 20 percent thallium and the electronic heat capacities of the normal metal are calculated from them.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Abstract of Stout & Guttman, Phys. Rev. 88, 703-712 (1952). Phase information from the Gunton thesis (Durham 1973, open PDF read in full): PDF p.12 (fct In-Tl up to 22.5 at.% Tl at room temperature) and PDF p.34 (thesis p.22, which cites the Tc-composition studies but gives no Tc values).
readerA.phase_or_sample: Single-phase face-centred tetragonal (indium) solid solution. Stout & Guttman measured a single crystal of exactly 5 at.% Tl.
readerA.measurement_method: Magnetic induction and electrical resistance against temperature and field (Stout & Guttman abstract)
readerA.evidence_note: Strongest lead of the six, but the rule is not met. (1) Stout & Guttman's abstract names a 5 at.% Tl single crystal and says critical fields for destroying superconductivity are given for 0-20 at.% Tl, so the sample superconducts. No Tc number appears in any text I could read. (2) Merriam, Hagen & Luo, Phys. Rev. 154, 424 (1967) (DOI 10.1103/physrev.154.424, Crossref-verified), abstract only: over 75 samples across the whole range; in the tetragonal phase Tc falls only slowly as Tl rises; there is a Tc anomaly at 4.4 at.% Tl; the tetragonal/cubic two-phase region lies at 30.1-31.7 at.% Tl. So 5 at.% Tl sits well inside the single-phase fct field. (3) Gubser, Mapother & Connelly, PRB 2, 2547 (1970), abstract: In-Tl alloys from 0 to 7% Tl measured down to 0.35 K, with Tc changes observed; no sample list or values. Expected Tc is about 3.3-3.4 K, but no paper text I read states it. The APS full texts could not be reached: journals.aps.org returns a proxy 403, and fetching the APS PDF through alphaXiv was refused by the permission classifier.
readerA.reason_if_not: The paper's own words show In-5 at.% Tl is superconducting, but no Tc for it is stated in any text I could read (abstracts only). The sample list and Tc-composition figure or table in Merriam 1967, Stout & Guttman 1952 and Gubser 1970 sit behind APS and were not readable here. The rule needs a stated Tc, or a bracketing series read from the figure or table.

readerA.quote: The solubility of Cd in Hg has been accurately determined; it is 1.5±0.25 at.% at 193°K. ... Boundaries of the ω phase occur at 88±1 at.% Hg at 193°K and at 35±2 at.% Hg at 383°K.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Abstract of Claeson, Luo & Merriam, Phys. Rev. 141, 412-418 (1966)
readerA.phase_or_sample: Hg0.95Cd0.05 is two-phase (alpha-Hg solid solution plus omega phase) at 193 K: it is past the 1.5 at.% Cd solubility limit and short of the omega boundary at 12 at.% Cd.
readerA.evidence_note: The abstract says Tc was measured 'covering the complete composition range', but its own phase boundaries put 5 at.% Cd in the alpha-Hg + omega two-phase field. A sample there would show the Tc of whichever phase carries the current (alpha-Hg near 4.15 K, or omega), not a single-phase alloy Tc. The full text with the sample list and Tc table is on APS, which was blocked (proxy 403).
readerA.reason_if_not: Two-phase composition beyond the Cd-in-Hg solubility limit, so the series condition fails. The direct condition (a Tc stated for Hg-5 at.% Cd) could not be checked because the full text was not reachable.

readerA.quote: In order to achieve improvements in superconducting properties of the Ti-Nb superconductor, effects of teruary [sic] additions of Hf have been studied on 42 Ti-Nb-Hf alloys with compositions of 25~65at.%Nb, 0~15at.%Hf and the balance Ti. Critical temperatures are found to depend upon Hf addition and aging temperature. In as-rolled Ti-40at.%Nb-3at.%Hf alloy the critical temperature is raised by about 0.3K over Ti-40at.%Nb alloy.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Katoh, Wada & Tachikawa, Denki-Seiko 53, 105-112 (1982), J-STAGE PDF: p.1 synopsis; p.4 Fig. 5 caption 'Critical temperature of as-rolled Ti-Nb-Hf alloys studied' (the figure values and the Japanese body text did not extract). Hawksworth & Larbalestier, IEEE Trans. Magn. 17, 49 (1981), DOI 10.1109/tmag.1981.1061177 (Crossref-verified, full text read): Figs. 1-2, Hc2 of Nb-Ti-Hf alloys on a ternary plot.
readerA.phase_or_sample: bcc beta Ti-Nb-Hf, as-rolled (Katoh et al.); arc-melted wire recrystallized at 875 °C and water-quenched (Hawksworth & Larbalestier)
readerA.measurement_method: Tc method not readable (Katoh et al.). Hawksworth & Larbalestier: resistive Hc2, first onset of resistance at 0.05 A/mm2.
readerA.synthesis_conditions: Hawksworth & Larbalestier: arc-melted in Ar, homogenized 8 h at 1350 °C, cold-rolled about 75%, recrystallized 1 h at 875 °C, water-quenched, Cu-sheathed and drawn to 1 mm wire
readerA.evidence_note: Ti64Nb32Hf4 falls inside the 42-alloy grid of Katoh/Wada/Tachikawa (the same work as Wada, Tachikawa & Kato, IEEE Trans. Magn. 17 (1981), DOI 10.1109/tmag.1981.1060925, which is paywalled). The only Tc statement in readable text is a relative one for Ti-40Nb-3Hf, 8 at.% Nb away. Hawksworth & Larbalestier show Nb-Ti-Hf alloys with Hc2(4.2 K) of 8.7-11.0 T, which implies Tc > 4.2 K, across the Ti80Nb20/Ti40Hf40Nb20/Ti40Nb60 region. The only composition named in their text is Ti60-Nb35-Hf5 (Hc2(2 K) = 14.5 T), which is 4 at.% Ti, 3 at.% Nb and 1 at.% Hf away, and no Tc is given. Physically this alloy almost certainly superconducts near 9 K, but no paper text read here says so.
readerA.reason_if_not: No readable text gives a Tc within 0.15 at.% of Ti64Nb32Hf4. The sample list and Fig. 5 Tc values (Katoh et al.) could not be extracted, so bracketing within 2 at.% cannot be checked. The IEEE version is paywalled.

readerA.quote: The composition dependence of the superconducting transition temperature Tc has been measured for the solid-solution range of the system Ta–Ti. Tc values, determined resistively for heavily cold-worked wire specimens, varied smoothly with composition, exhibiting a maximum of 8.8°K corresponding to a valence-electron-to-atom ratio of 4.5.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Abstract of Colling, Ralls & Wulff, J. Appl. Phys. 37, 4750-4752 (1966). Also read in full: Suenaga & Ralls, UCRL-18276-Rev (= J. Appl. Phys. 40, 4457 (1969), DOI 10.1063/1.1657215, Crossref-verified), PDF pp.5-8 and Fig. 1 (ternary Tc map that includes binary Ti-Ta data from Colling et al.; values illegible in the extraction). Prekul, Rassokhin & Volkenshtein, Sov. Phys. JETP 40, 1134 (1975) (no Crossref DOI), pp.1134-1135 and Fig. 4 (Tc^s, Tc^f against concentration for TixTa1-x; data points not machine-readable).
readerA.phase_or_sample: bcc beta Ta-Ti solid solution; heavily cold-worked wire (Colling et al.); water-quenched from 1100 °C (Prekul et al.)
readerA.measurement_method: Resistive (Colling et al.); resistive onset and finish (Prekul et al.)
readerA.synthesis_conditions: Colling et al.: heavily cold-worked wire, with annealed samples giving lower Tc. Prekul et al.: quenched from 1100 °C into water.
readerA.evidence_note: Ta53Ti47 has e/a = 4.53, essentially at the reported Tc maximum (e/a 4.5, about Ta50Ti50, Tc 8.8 K in cold-worked wire). Prekul et al. state they measured Ti-Ta 'in the entire range of concentrations where quenching fixes a beta-solid solution with bcc structure', with Tc plotted in Fig. 4, but neither the sample compositions nor the Tc values are in text form. Suenaga & Ralls note that Neuringer & Shapira studied Ti-52 at.% Ta (Hc2), which is about 1 at.% off and gives no Tc in the text read. Strong lead: Colling 1966 Table/Fig. or Prekul Fig. 4, read as images, would very likely settle it.
readerA.reason_if_not: The abstract says only that Tc 'varied smoothly with composition'. The Colling full text (AIP) was not reachable, and in the two open full texts the Ti-Ta Tc data exist only as figures that could not be read. So neither a stated Tc for Ta53Ti47 nor a bracketing sample list was obtained.

readerA.quote: Superconducting transition temperatures (Tc) have been measured on a series of chemically vapour-deposited (CVD) tungsten-rhenium alloys. The samples were prepared by hydrogen reduction of tungsten and rhenium hexafluoride in the composition range 3·5 to 95 at.-% Re.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Abstract of Easton, Koch, Kroeger & Cable, Phil. Mag. 30, 1117-1134 (1974). Also the abstract of Hulm & Blaugher, Phys. Rev. 123, 1569 (1961), DOI 10.1103/physrev.123.1569.
readerA.phase_or_sample: bcc W-Re solid solution expected at 10 at.% Re; the CVD deposits contained metastable phases and trapped impurities
readerA.synthesis_conditions: CVD by H2 reduction of WF6/ReF6 (Easton et al.); high-temperature annealing lowered Tc to the arc-melted values
readerA.evidence_note: Easton et al. covered 3.5-95 at.% Re, but as-deposited CVD Tc values were enhanced above arc-melted ones by metastable A15 phases and trapped impurities. A W-10Re CVD value would therefore not be a clean bulk equilibrium Tc even if found. The Hulm & Blaugher abstract (solid solutions tested down to 1 K; Tc maxima near e/a 4.7 and 6.4; W0.9Re0.1 has e/a 6.1) gives no compositions or values. An open arXiv full text (arXiv:2510.18696, W0.75Re0.25 films) cites only bulk W0.75Re0.25 Tc values (alpha about 5 K, beta about 10 K), which are 15 at.% away. No open-access primary text with a W-rich W-Re Tc was found.
readerA.reason_if_not: No text read states a Tc for W-10 at.% Re or gives a bracketing sample list. The primary sources (Easton 1974, Hulm & Blaugher 1961) are paywalled and their abstracts lack compositions and Tc values.

readerA.quote: Table I: "Zr70 V30 8.4 5.0 6.6 hcp, bee [bcc], ZrV2" (Tc ind onset, Tc ind midpoint, Tc R midpoint in K; phases present). Text: "Previous work [13] on hcp Zr-V and Hf-V as well as the corresponding bcc solid solution has shown that they are not superconducting down to 4.2°K." and "heat treating at temperatures greater than 300°C eventually leads to the formation of ZrV2 and hcp Zr. This is to be expected since these are the equilibrium phases for this system"
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Tenhover, CALT-822-111 (Caltech/DOE report, 1979). Report p.5 Table I (PDF p.10); pp.6-7 (PDF pp.11-12) on hcp/bcc Zr-V being non-superconducting and superconductivity coming from ZrV2; p.12 (PDF p.17) on equilibrium phases hcp Zr + ZrV2.
readerA.phase_or_sample: The equilibrium Zr-rich alloy is two-phase (hcp alpha-Zr + C15 ZrV2). The nearest measured sample, splat-cooled Zr70V30, was multiphase (mostly hcp, some bcc, a trace of ZrV2).
readerA.measurement_method: Inductive (ac bridge) and resistive (four-probe) Tc, onset and midpoint
readerA.synthesis_conditions: Levitation-melted under Ar, splat-cooled in He into foils about 30 µm thick; some foils heat-treated for 24 h at 200-600 °C
readerA.evidence_note: Zr75V25 is not in Tenhover's sample list. The nearest sample is Zr70V30 (5 at.% V off). It superconducts with an 8.4 K inductive onset, but the author attributes this to the ZrV2 Laves phase: 'the only supercurrent carrying phase present at 4.2°K is ZrV2'. Ref. [13] is Pollock, Shull & Gatos, phys. stat. sol. (a) 2, 251 (1970), DOI 10.1002/pssa.19700020209, abstract only: Zr-6 and 9 at.% V alloys age to alpha-Zr + V2Zr. The arXiv full text 1908.10570 (as-cast V1-xZrx) covers only x ≤ 0.4, the V-rich side, and finds multiphase samples.
readerA.reason_if_not: No sample within 0.15 at.% of Zr75V25 is reported. The alloy is two-phase (alpha-Zr + ZrV2), so the series condition fails, and the Zr-V solid solutions themselves are reported non-superconducting above 4.2 K. Any superconductivity of a Zr3V bulk sample would come from the ZrV2 second phase.

readerB.quote: The superconducting transition temperatures of over 75 samples spanning the entire composition range of the indium-thallium alloy system have been measured. [...] In all phases, Tc decreases with increasing Tl content, the rate of decrease in the tetragonal (indium) phase being, however, much less steep than in the other phases. [...] An anomaly in the Tc-versus-composition plot at 4.4 at.% Tl is extremely similar in form to one previously identified in In-Cd as a Brillouin-zone effect. (Merriam, Hagen and Luo, Phys. Rev. 154, 424 (1967), abstract; TeX markup removed)
readerB.page_table_or_figure: Abstract only (Phys. Rev. 154, 424-435). I could not read the sample list or the Tc-versus-composition figure.
readerB.phase_or_sample: Tetragonal (fct) In-based solid solution, expected to be single phase at 5 at.% Tl. Gunton thesis (Durham 1973) p.12: fct at room temperature up to 22.5 at.% Tl. Larbalestier thesis (Imperial 1970) pp.65-66, citing Pollock and King: at 9.5 K every alloy below 28.75 at.% Tl is tetragonal.
readerB.reason_if_not: I could not open the primary full texts. journals.aps.org and doi.org are refused by this session's proxy, and the APS papers are paywalled. So I have no sample list and no figure that brackets 5 at.% Tl within 2 at.%, and no sentence that states a Tc for In-5 at.% Tl. The rule says an abstract claiming the 'entire composition range' is not enough. Three open theses were read in full (fetched with the alphaXiv reader because the hosts block curl), but none brackets this composition. Pollock (Imperial 1967), Table 20, p.126: the lowest-Tl sample is 15.2 at.% Tl, Tc 3.295 K, which is 10 at.% away. Larbalestier (1970) covers only 26-33 at.% Tl. Gunton (1973) has no Tc data.
readerB.evidence_note: Very likely a wrong negative, but not confirmed under the rule. Leads for a reader who has APS access: (1) Merriam et al. 1967. Its abstract places a Tc-versus-composition anomaly at 4.4 at.% Tl, so dense sampling around 4-5 at.% Tl is implied. (2) Gubser, Mapother and Connelly, Phys. Rev. B 2, 2547 (1970), DOI 10.1103/physrevb.2.2547 (Crossref-registered). Its abstract reports critical-field measurements down to 0.35 K on In-Tl alloys 'covering the concentration range of 0-7% Tl'. That is likely a single-phase bracketing series, but the sample list was not read. (3) Love, Callen and Nix, Phys. Rev. 87, 844 (1952), DOI 10.1103/physrev.87.844 (Crossref-registered). According to the Larbalestier thesis p.78 (secondary), this study included 5, 10, 15, 20, 28.5 and 37 at.% Tl superconducting alloys measured as spheres. Pollock (1967) Table 20 gives Tc, measured by a.c. induction, of 3.295 K at 15.2 at.% Tl, 3.290 K at 17.1 and 3.285 K at 18.9. Indium itself is 3.4 K. So the expected Tc at 5 at.% Tl is about 3.3-3.4 K, but this is an inference, not a reading.
readerB.measurement_method: Primary source (not read): Tc by inductive/magnetic methods per the abstract. Secondary context (Pollock): a.c. mutual inductance, 0.24 G field, midpoint of transition.

readerB.quote: The superconducting transition temperatures of Cd-Hg alloys covering the complete composition range have been determined. The solubility of Cd in Hg has been accurately determined; it is 1.5±0.25 at.% at 193°K. [...] Boundaries of the ω phase occur at 88±1 at.% Hg at 193°K and at 35±2 at.% Hg at 383°K. (Claeson, Luo and Merriam, Phys. Rev. 141, 412 (1966), abstract; TeX markup removed)
readerB.page_table_or_figure: Abstract only (Phys. Rev. 141, 412-418). I could not read the sample table or the Tc-versus-composition figure.
readerB.phase_or_sample: Two-phase by the paper's own boundaries. At 193 K the Hg terminal solid solution ends at 1.5 at.% Cd (98.5 at.% Hg) and the omega phase begins at 88 at.% Hg. So Hg0.95Cd0.05 lies in the Hg(Cd) plus omega two-phase field.
readerB.reason_if_not: The series condition cannot apply, because the composition lies beyond the 1.5 at.% solubility limit of Cd in Hg, in a two-phase field. The only remaining route is a sentence or table entry in the paper that gives a Tc for a sample at 95 at.% Hg (within 0.15 at.%). The full text is paywalled and unreachable from this session (journals.aps.org and doi.org are refused by the proxy), so no such entry could be read.
readerB.evidence_note: Both constituents of a two-phase Hg-5Cd sample are expected to superconduct: Hg at about 4.15 K and the omega phase at an unknown Tc. A measured sample would very likely show a transition. But the owner's rule does not accept a two-phase composition unless the paper itself reports that composition, so this stays at not_confirmed until someone reads the paper's sample table. No open-access copy, thesis or report version was found through FastTrack or alphaXiv.

readerB.reason_if_not: I found no paper, open or abstract, that reports Ti0.64Nb0.32Hf0.04, or a Nb-Ti-Hf series bracketing it within 2 at.% on each element. FastTrack searches (Nb-Ti-Hf ternary superconducting properties; hafnium addition NbTi Hc2 Tc; Ti-Nb-Hf upper critical field) and alphaXiv searches (Nb-Ti-Hf, Ti-Nb-Hf, NbTi) returned only Nb-rich binaries (Nb0.85X0.15, arXiv:2512.18821) and multi-element high-entropy alloys far from this composition. The 1960s-1980s Nb-Ti-Hf alloy literature is not indexed with abstracts in these sources, and no open full text was found.
readerB.evidence_note: From physics knowledge only, not a reading: Ti-rich bcc Nb-Ti near Ti0.64Nb0.36 superconducts at about 8-9.5 K, and a 4 at.% Hf substitution would not be expected to destroy superconductivity. Quenched Ti-rich beta alloys can contain omega or alpha'' phases, so the sample's phase state also matters. A reader with access to the metallurgical journals (Trans. AIME, J. Less-Common Met., Kharkov/Japanese Nb-Ti-Hf studies) is needed.

readerB.page_table_or_figure: Lead only: D. A. Colling, K. M. Ralls and J. Wulff, 'High-field superconductivity of tantalum-titanium alloys', Trans. Metall. Soc. AIME 236 (August 1966); OSTI IDs 7351757 and 4513266, NSA-20-037268. It has no DOI, and the OSTI record has no abstract or full text.
readerB.phase_or_sample: bcc beta solid solution expected at 53 at.% Ta (single phase), but not verified from a source.
readerB.reason_if_not: I found no readable text that gives a Tc for Ta0.53Ti0.47, or a Ta-Ti series bracketing it within 2 at.%. The only Ta-Ti-specific lead is the Colling, Ralls and Wulff 1966 paper, and OSTI holds its citation only. Hulm and Blaugher, Phys. Rev. 123, 1569 (1961), DOI 10.1103/physrev.123.1569 (Crossref bibliographic match on authors, volume and pages), tested transition-metal solid solutions down to 1 K, including pairs from different rows. Its abstract does not say whether Ta-Ti was included, and the full text is paywalled and unreachable. alphaXiv searches found only Ta-Hf/Ta-Zr (arXiv:2306.10438), Ta-Hf films and high-entropy alloys, with no binary Ta-Ti data.
readerB.evidence_note: From physics knowledge only: Ta (4.4 K) and bcc Ti-rich alloys both superconduct, so a bcc Ta-47Ti alloy is very likely a superconductor of a few K. Not verified under the rule. Next step: obtain Colling et al. (Trans. AIME 1966) or Hulm and Blaugher (1961) through a library.

readerB.quote: Superconducting transition temperatures (Tc) have been measured on a series of chemically vapour-deposited (CVD) tungsten-rhenium alloys. The samples were prepared by hydrogen reduction of tungsten and rhenium hexafluoride in the composition range 3·5 to 95 at.-% Re. [...] The transition temperatures of asdeposited samples were higher than those of comparable arc-melted alloys for the entire composition range regardless of crystal structure. (Easton, Koch, Kroeger and Cable, Philos. Mag. 30, 1117 (1974), abstract)
readerB.page_table_or_figure: Abstract only (Philos. Mag. 30(5), 1117-1134). I could not read the sample list or the Tc-versus-composition table or figure.
readerB.phase_or_sample: bcc alpha-W(Re) solid solution expected at 10 at.% Re for arc-melted material. The CVD deposits in Easton et al. may contain metastable A15 phase and trapped impurities (per their abstract).
readerB.reason_if_not: The abstract gives no Tc at 10 at.% Re and no sample list. The only general statement covers a 3.5-95 at.% Re range, which is not enough under the rule. The as-deposited CVD samples are reported as metastable or impurity-enhanced, so even a 10 at.% Re CVD value would need checking against the annealed or arc-melted data in the full text. The full text (Taylor and Francis) is paywalled and unreachable here. Hulm and Blaugher 1961 (10.1103/physrev.123.1569) measured W-group solid solutions, but only down to 1 K. W-rich W-Re close to tungsten (Tc about 0.015 K) could lie below such a floor, so the training label 0 may come from a 'not superconducting above about 1 K' result. That could not be checked.
readerB.evidence_note: Lead found through the reference list of arXiv:2510.18696 (W0.75Re0.25 films), which I read in full. That paper cites Easton et al. for bulk W-Re Tc and states that bulk alpha-W0.75Re0.25 has Tc about 5 K. Its own data are on films only, so it is not evidence for W0.9Re0.1. Whether bcc W-10 at.% Re superconducts above about 1 K is genuinely uncertain. This row should not be corrected without the primary table.

readerB.quote: We report here the structural, electrical and magnetic properties of as-cast V1-xZrx alloys (x = 0 - 0.4) at low temperatures. We observe that all the alloys undergo successive peritectic and eutectic reactions during cooling from the melt which leads to the formation of five phases [...] The β-V and ZrV2 phases show superconductivity below 5.3 K and 8.5 K respectively. (arXiv:1908.07288, abstract)
readerB.page_table_or_figure: Abstract only. This is the nearest Zr-V study found, and its composition range (Zr at most 40 at.%) does not reach Zr 75 at.%.
readerB.phase_or_sample: Multi-phase expected at Zr0.75V0.25: alpha/beta-Zr plus ZrV2 Laves phase, from the eutectic Zr-V system. This is consistent with the five-phase as-cast microstructures reported for x up to 0.4.
readerB.reason_if_not: I found no paper that reports Zr0.75V0.25 itself as superconducting, and the composition is multi-phase, so the series condition cannot apply. The nearest study stops at x = 0.4 Zr. Its arXiv DOI (10.48550/arxiv.1908.07288) is not registered with Crossref; it is a DataCite arXiv DOI. FastTrack and alphaXiv searches for Zr-rich Zr-V superconductivity returned nothing else relevant.
readerB.evidence_note: A Zr-25V sample would hold roughly 37% of its atoms in ZrV2, which superconducts at 8.5 K, so a measured sample would likely show a percolating or partial transition. Under the owner's rule that does not count unless a paper reports this composition as superconducting. Keep label 0.

verified.quote: Single crystal specimens of composition 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20 atom percent thallium, and polycrystalline specimens containing 15, 20, 38, and 50 percent thallium, were investigated. ... The critical fields for destruction of superconductivity are given for the range 0 to 20 percent thallium (Stout & Guttman, Phys. Rev. 88, 703 (1952), abstract)
verified.page_table_or_figure: Abstract only, Phys. Rev. 88, 703-712. Also the abstracts of Merriam, Hagen & Luo, Phys. Rev. 154, 424-435 (1967), DOI 10.1103/physrev.154.424, and Gubser, Mapother & Connelly, PRB 2, 2547 (1970), DOI 10.1103/physrevb.2.2547. Both DOIs were re-checked against Crossref.
verified.phase_or_sample: fct (indium) solid solution, single phase at 5 at.% Tl. Merriam et al. put the tetragonal/cubic two-phase region at 30.1-31.7 at.% Tl. Stout & Guttman measured a single crystal of exactly 5 at.% Tl.
verified.measurement_method: Magnetic induction and electrical resistance against temperature and field (Stout & Guttman abstract)
verified.verifier_reason: Neither reader confirmed the row, so it cannot be applied. I re-opened the three abstracts and the Crossref records, and both readers' quotes and DOIs are accurate. The 5 at.% Tl sample is shown to superconduct (critical fields are given for 0-20% Tl), but no text I could reach gives its Tc. The Merriam abstract claims the 'entire composition range' and gives only the overall Tc span (2.5-3.8 K) and a 4.4 at.% Tl anomaly, which the rule says is not enough. The sample list or Tc figure that would bracket 5 at.% within 2 at.% was not read. journals.aps.org is refused by the proxy. I did not try to fetch the paywalled APS full texts through a third-party reader.
verified.reason_if_not: No Tc is stated for In0.95Tl0.05 in any readable text, and no sample list or Tc-composition figure that brackets it was read. Strongest lead: Stout & Guttman 1952 or Merriam 1967 full text (Tc table), which needs APS access.
verified.evidence_note: Very likely a wrong negative, with Tc expected near 3.3-3.4 K, but that is an inference. Reader A used Stout & Guttman and Reader B used Merriam. The two leads differ but do not conflict.

verified.quote: The superconducting transition temperatures of Cd-Hg alloys covering the complete composition range have been determined. The solubility of Cd in Hg has been accurately determined; it is 1.5±0.25 at.% at 193°K. ... Boundaries of the ω phase occur at 88±1 at.% Hg at 193°K and at 35±2 at.% Hg at 383°K. (Claeson, Luo & Merriam, Phys. Rev. 141, 412 (1966), abstract)
verified.page_table_or_figure: Abstract only, Phys. Rev. 141, 412-418 (Crossref: Claeson, Luo, Merriam, vol. 141, issue 1, 1966)
verified.phase_or_sample: Two-phase by the paper's own boundaries. At 193 K, 95 at.% Hg lies between the Hg terminal solid solution (ending at 98.5 at.% Hg) and the omega phase (starting at 88 at.% Hg).
verified.verifier_reason: Neither reader confirmed the row, so it cannot be applied. I checked the abstract myself and the readers' numbers are right: Cd solubility in Hg is 1.5±0.25 at.% and the omega boundary is at 88±1 at.% Hg, both at 193 K. Hg0.95Cd0.05 is therefore in a two-phase field and the series condition fails. The only other route would be a table entry for a 95 at.% Hg sample, and the APS full text was unreachable (proxy 403). A two-phase sample's transition would also come from whichever phase percolates (Hg near 4.15 K or omega), not from a single-phase alloy at this composition.
verified.reason_if_not: Two-phase composition beyond the solubility limit, so the series condition fails. No direct Tc for Hg-5 at.% Cd was read.
verified.evidence_note: Both readers read the same abstract and reached the same phase conclusion. No open-access copy was found.

verified.quote: At 2 K, however, there is a small increase in μoHc2 from 14.2 T in the binary alloys to 14.5 T for an alloy of composition Nb60 at% Ti 5 at% Hf (Nb41wt%Ti13wt%Hf). (Hawksworth & Larbalestier, IEEE Trans. Magn. 17, 49 (1981), p.50)
verified.page_table_or_figure: Hawksworth & Larbalestier, IEEE Trans. verified.verifier_reason: Neither reader confirmed the row. I re-read the Hawksworth & Larbalestier full text. The only named Nb-Ti-Hf composition is 'Nb60 at% Ti 5 at% Hf (Nb41wt%Ti13wt%Hf)', and converting the wt% gives Ti60.1 Nb34.7 Hf5.1. That is about 4 at.% Ti and 3 at.% Nb off Ti64Nb32Hf4, outside 0.15 at.%. The paper says Tc was measured but prints no Tc values, and the Fig. 1-2 point values cannot be assigned to compositions from the extracted text. Hc2(4.2 K) > 0 implies Tc > 4.2 K, but the rule needs a stated Tc. The Katoh et al. 42-alloy grid (25-65 Nb, 0-15 Hf) may bracket the composition, but its sample list and Fig. 5 values were not readable.
verified.reason_if_not: No stated Tc within 0.15 at.% of Ti64Nb32Hf4, and no bracketing sample list was read.
verified.evidence_note: Reader A's reading of Ti60-Nb35-Hf5 is correct; I checked it from the wt% conversion. Reader B found no source. Physically the alloy very likely superconducts near 8-9 K, but that is not shown under the rule.

verified.quote: The composition dependence of the superconducting transition temperature Tc has been measured for the solid-solution range of the system Ta–Ti. Tc values, determined resistively for heavily cold-worked wire specimens, varied smoothly with composition, exhibiting a maximum of 8.8°K corresponding to a valence-electron-to-atom ratio of 4.5. Little sharpening of transitions was found for annealed samples, and lower values of Tc were obtained. (Colling, Ralls & Wulff, J. Appl. Phys. 37, 4750 (1966), abstract)
verified.phase_or_sample: bcc beta Ta-Ti solid solution; heavily cold-worked wire; annealed samples gave lower Tc
verified.verifier_reason: Neither reader confirmed the row. The abstract, which I re-read, gives only the Tc maximum (8.8 K at e/a 4.5, near Ta50Ti50) and says Tc 'varied smoothly'. It gives no sample list and no Tc for Ta53Ti47. The Tc it does report comes from heavily cold-worked wire, and annealing lowered it, so even a value read off the figure would need the annealed (equilibrium) value checked. The open full texts Reader A used (Suenaga & Ralls; Prekul et al.) hold the Ti-Ta data only as figures that could not be read. Reader B found no readable source.
verified.reason_if_not: No stated Tc for Ta0.53Ti0.47 and no bracketing sample list was read. The source is abstract only.
verified.evidence_note: Strong lead: Colling et al. 1966 (Tc-composition figure or table) or Prekul et al. 1975 Fig. 4, read as images. The Ta53Ti47 Tc is likely 7-9 K, but this is not verified.

verified.quote: The samples were prepared by hydrogen reduction of tungsten and rhenium hexafluoride in the composition range 3·5 to 95 at.-% Re. ... The transition temperatures of asdeposited samples were higher than those of comparable arc-melted alloys for the entire composition range regardless of crystal structure. ... After high-temperature annealing the T c was decreased to that of arc-melted samples. (Easton, Koch, Kroeger & Cable, Phil. Mag. 30, 1117 (1974), abstract)
verified.page_table_or_figure: Abstract only, Phil. Mag. 30(5), 1117-1134. Also Hulm & Blaugher, Phys. Rev. 123, 1569-1580 (1961), DOI 10.1103/physrev.123.1569 (Crossref-verified), title and abstract only.
verified.phase_or_sample: bcc W(Re) solid solution expected for equilibrium material at 10 at.% Re. The as-deposited CVD samples are metastable or carry trapped impurities, by the paper's own account.
verified.synthesis_conditions: CVD by H2 reduction of WF6 and ReF6; high-temperature annealing returned Tc to the arc-melted values
verified.verifier_reason: Neither reader confirmed the row. The abstract gives no Tc at 10 at.% Re and no sample list. It also states that as-deposited CVD Tc values are enhanced above equilibrium arc-melted values by metastable A15 phase or trapped impurities. A CVD W-10Re value would therefore be a non-equilibrium Tc, the kind of impurity- or metastable-phase superconductivity the rule should exclude. Only the annealed or arc-melted value would count. Hulm & Blaugher's abstract gives no W-Re compositions or values.
verified.reason_if_not: No stated Tc for W0.9Re0.1 and no bracketing series was read. The available CVD data are reported as metastable or impurity-enhanced.
verified.evidence_note: Whether bcc W-10 at.% Re superconducts above about 1 K is genuinely uncertain (W itself is about 0.015 K). Do not correct this row without the annealed or arc-melted table.

Text: "Previous work [13] on hcp Zr-V and Hf-V as well as the corresponding bcc solid solution has shown that they are not superconducting down to 4.2°K." and "strongly suggest that the only supercurrent carrying phase present at 4.2°K is ZrV2." verified.page_table_or_figure: Tenhover, CALT-822-111 (OSTI report, 1979): report p.5 Table I (PDF p.10), pp.6-7 (PDF pp.11-12), p.12 (PDF p.17). Also arXiv:1908.07288 (as-cast V1-xZrx, x = 0-0.4), pp.1-4 and Table I.
verified.phase_or_sample: Equilibrium Zr-rich Zr-V is two-phase (hcp alpha-Zr + C15 ZrV2). Zr75V25 is not in any sample list read. The nearest sample, splat-cooled Zr70V30 foil about 30 µm thick, was multiphase and non-equilibrium.
verified.measurement_method: Inductive (ac bridge) and four-probe resistive Tc, onset and midpoint
verified.synthesis_conditions: Levitation-melted under Ar, splat-cooled in He into foils about 30 µm thick
verified.verifier_reason: Neither reader confirmed the row. I re-read the Tenhover report in full, and Reader A's table entry and quotes are accurate. Zr75V25 was not measured. The nearest sample (Zr70V30) is 5 at.% V away, is a splat-quenched multiphase foil rather than an equilibrium bulk sample, and owes its superconductivity to the ZrV2 impurity phase; the Zr-V solid solutions are reported non-superconducting down to 4.2 K. arXiv:1908.07288 (Reader B's lead, which I re-read) covers only x ≤ 0.40 Zr and finds five-phase as-cast samples. Its arXiv DOI is a DataCite DOI, not a Crossref one, as Reader B noted. Reader A's arXiv:1908.10570 is a real companion paper on the same alloys (heat conduction).
verified.reason_if_not: Two-phase composition, so the series condition fails. No sample within 0.15 at.% was reported, and any superconductivity would come from the ZrV2 second phase.
verified.evidence_note: The label 0 is consistent with the rule. A Zr-25V sample would likely show a partial or percolating ZrV2 transition near 8.5 K, but that is second-phase superconductivity.
